Figure 4: Leaky ReLU activations in the readout result in marginally slower and less stable training, with delayed plateauing of both the validation loss and evaluation metric at larger values.
Figure 5: Replacing tanh activation functions in the readout results in increased roughness and prediction variance, but the model maintains its strong predictive ability.
Figure 6: Reducing the sample size only marginally degrades training and performance in absolute terms.
Figure 8: Although small in absolute terms, increasing spatial data sparsity has the greatest impact on both training speed and stability, as well as its predictive performance.
